for current well-being or post-traumatic growth. Open-ended questions thus capture valuable information that standard questionnaires miss, and we recommend including them routinely and analysing the responses.

articles_hidden.title: Humans’ reasons for and against eating animals
articles_hidden.authors: Christopher James Hopwood
articles_hidden.abstract:
Humans offer a wide range of reasons for and against eating animals. These reasons predict dietary
behavior, yet they often fail to translate into consistent action, and experimentally altering reasons
rarely produces durable changes in consumption. Reasons for and against eating animals are not
opposites, and many humans maintain conflicting reasons, which often leads to dissonance reducing
strategies. Developmental evidence suggests that concern for animals declines from childhood to
adulthood, while cross-cultural work reveals systematic variation in which reasons are prioritized.
Together, this literature highlights both the stability and the malleability of reasoning about food and
provides a window into how individuals reconcile beliefs with everyday practices. Understanding
these patterns also has practical implications for interventions aimed at promoting animal welfare,
social justice, and planetary health.

articles_hidden.title: Development of Visual Temporal Order Judgment and Its Relationship to Sensory Processing Characteristics in Children
articles_hidden.authors: Ryoichi Watanabe; Nozomi Yamamoto; Takeshi Atsumi; Masakazu Ide
articles_hidden.abstract: Accurate temporal order processing is fundamental to perception, action, and learning; however, less is known about visual temporal order judgment (TOJ) development than about auditory temporal processing development. Here, we examined visual TOJ in children and adults, focusing on two forms of temporal order processing—judgments about stimulus color and about spatial location—and the association of individual sensory profile differences with TOJ performance. Participants (adults and children aged 4–6-, 7–9, and 10–12 years) completed two visual TOJ tasks, namely a color task in which they judged which color appeared first, and a spatial task in which they judged which location was stimulated first. Performance was analyzed using trial-level accuracy and 75% correct thresholds estimated from anchored psychometric functions. Accuracy improved and thresholds decreased with age, indicating developmental improvements in visual-temporal order processing. Performance was better on the spatial task than on the color task, indicating greater difficulty judging the temporal order of the stimulus color than that of the spatial location. Exploratory analyses yielded mixed evidence for the variance of the color-spatial difference across age groups; accuracy analysis revealed a significant age group × task interaction, whereas threshold analysis did not. Short Sensory Profile scores were not robustly associated with TOJ thresholds in either children or adults. Overall, the findings indicate that visual temporal order processing continues to develop throughout childhood and that task demands influence TOJ performance; its relationship with broader sensory processing characteristics appears limited or more complex in typically developing participants.

articles_hidden.title: The Dual Nature of Syntactic Node Count: Facilitating and Inhibiting Sentence Comprehension
articles_hidden.authors: Kohei Kajikawa; Shinnosuke Isono
articles_hidden.abstract: Neurolinguistic research on syntactic processing has used Node Count, the number of syntactic nodes assumed to be built at each word, to investigate how structure-building effort affects brain activity. However, several recent studies cast doubt on the presumed link between Node Count and processing effort; they observe negative correlations between Node Count and reading times. These facilitatory effects raise an alternative hypothesis: rather than reflecting structure-building effort, Node Count may index structure-mediated predictability. To test this hypothesis, we first relate Node Count to an information-theoretic measure of contextual support, the pointwise mutual information (PMI) between a word and its context. We then evaluate the relationship between Node Count and reading times from three large-scale naturalistic English datasets. For these analyses, we derive Node Count under three grammar formalisms (phrase-structure grammar, dependency grammar, and combinatory categorial grammar) and multiple parsing strategies. Variants whose count reflects integrative parsing steps correlate positively with PMI and show a dual behavioral profile: robust facilitation in immediate regions, consistent with structure-mediated predictability, and a delayed slowdown in spillover regions, most consistent with the cost of contextual semantic integration. The facilitatory effect explains reading-time variance beyond GPT-2 surprisal, indicating that Node Count has unique psycholinguistic value as an index of human prediction. These results highlight the role of structural representations in human language processing and underscore the need for a careful interpretation of the observed correlations between Node Count and brain activity in neurolinguistic studies.

articles_hidden.title: 사회적 참사 맥락에서 정서적 안전은 어떻게 측정될 수 있는가: 정서적 안전 및 근접 개념 측정도구에 대한 주제범위 문헌고찰
articles_hidden.authors: jae Choi
articles_hidden.abstract:
초록
목적: 본 연구는 정서적 안전(emotional safety)과 그 근접 개념인 정서적 안정감(emotional security), 안전감(sense of safety)을 측정하는 도구를 체계적으로 지도화하고, 사회적 참사 피해자와 지역사회에 적용할 때의 개념적·측정적 공백을 규명하고자 하였다.
방법: JBI 주제범위 문헌고찰 방법론과 PRISMA-ScR 지침을 따랐다. PubMed, SocINDEX with Full Text, Google Scholar, RISS, KISS, DBpia, e-article을 2026년 11월 12일에 검색하고 인용추적을 병행하였다. 정서적 안전 및 근접 개념을 전체 척도 또는 명명된 하위척도로 측정하고 심리측정적 근거를 보고한 개발·타당화·번안 연구를 포함하였다.
결과: 데이터베이스에서 689편이 검색되었고 중복 제거 후 587편을 선별하여 13편, 인용추적으로 2편을 추가해 총 15편(12개 도구)을 분석하였다. 정서적 안전을 명시한 연구는 4편이었고 독립 척도는 소아 환자 선별도구 1개뿐이었다. 도구의 맥락은 의료(4편), 일반 성인·종사자(4편), 가족(3편), 학교·청소년 프로그램(2편), 지역사회 폭력(1편), 기술 수용(1편)이었으며 재난이나 사회적 참사 맥락에서 개발·타당화된 도구는 없었다. 국내 연구는 신경지 기반 심리적 안전감 척도 번안 1편이었고, 국내 검색 결과의 약 3분의 1은 정서적 안전이 아닌 정서적 안정(emotional stability)을 다루어 용어 혼용이 확인되었다. 기존 도구는 신체적 안정, 관계적 수용, 기관 신뢰를 부분적으로 포착했으나 애도와 기억의 존중, 2차 피해로부터의 보호, 진실과 정보에 대한 접근, 집단적 안전감은 거의 다루지 않았다.
결론: 사회적 참사 맥락의 정서적 안전 측정은 사실상 공백 상태이다. 트라우마 인지 원칙과 참사 피해 당사자의 경험을 반영한 개념분석과 도구개발이 필요하며, 본 연구가 제안한 8개 예비 차원은 그 출발점으로 활용될 수 있다.

articles_hidden.title: Reverse-Engineering Speech and Music Categorization from a Single Sound Source
articles_hidden.authors: Lauren K Fink; Madita Hörster; David Poeppel; Melanie Wald-Fuhrmann; Pauline Larrouy-Maestri
articles_hidden.abstract: Classifying whether an auditory signal is music or speech is important for both humans and computational systems. Although previous literature suggests that music and speech are easily separable categories, common experimental approaches may bias findings toward this distinction by relying on stimuli from different sound sources and predefined response labels. Here, we use stimulus material from the dùndún drum – a speech surrogate that can signal either speech-related or musical content. We first replicate standard speech-music categorization results (N = 108). Then, we depart from the typical experimental procedure by asking new participants (N = 180) to sort and label the stimulus material, without predefined categories. Hierarchical clustering of participants’ stimulus groupings reveals multiple organizing dimensions, with the speech–music distinction reliably present but secondary under label-free conditions. By reverse-engineering the relationship between sorting behavior, acoustic features, and semantic labels, we characterize how speech–music categorization relates to other salient perceptual dimensions and how its behavioral prominence depends on task constraints.

articles_hidden.title: Reasoning about counterfactual choices and responsibility judgements in children
articles_hidden.authors: Shalini Gautam; Fiery Andrews Cushman
articles_hidden.abstract: Judgements of responsibility are foundational to human social life. Adults judge responsibility by considering not just what someone chose to do, but also the alternative choices available to them. Thus, the development of adult-like responsibility judgements in children depends on their capacity to reason about counterfactual choices. In this Review, we distinguish three key elements of this capacity: understanding that counterfactual choices are possible, successfully reasoning about counterfactual worlds, and identifying the most relevant counterfactuals in any given situation. This framework clarifies the relationship between counterfactual reasoning and responsibility judgements in childhood, identifies conceptually distinct elements of children’s understanding of responsibility, and opens up avenues for inquiry into an essential element of children’s social reasoning.

articles_hidden.title: How Daily Family Dynamics Become Developmental Change: A Cross-Timescale Framework for Parent–Adolescent Research
articles_hidden.authors: Kaiwen Bi; Mark S. Chen
articles_hidden.abstract: Intensive longitudinal studies link parent–adolescent daily emotions and behaviors, yet whether these fast dynamics shape lasting change remains a fundamental question. We propose a cross-timescale framework centered on parent–adolescent coupling: how one family member’s fluctuations track another’s. We first distinguish between- from within-family associations and review evidence showing that within-family findings vary by timescale. We then review literature linking short-term processes to long-term adjustment, identifying a greater focus on adults over adolescents despite rapid developmental change. From this literature, we review three methodological designs. The first tests whether more strongly coupled families experience worse adjustment with one burst of intensive assessment. The second asks whether coupling and adjustment change together across multiple bursts. The third tests whether unusually strong coupling within a family precedes worsening adjustment. We end by discussing how considering the context where the coupling unfolds and causal inference strengthens these designs, eventually informing family-based treatment.

articles_hidden.title: mPACT-MIS-v1.0: A Clinician–Informed Framework for Evaluating Epistemic Drift in Large Language Models
articles_hidden.authors: Alison Cerezo; Caraline Bruzinski; Shamal Lalvani; Valerie Jane Douglas; Kyle Etter; Logan Lake; Maggie Gorraiz; Megan Greenlaw; Alisa Breetz; Dogan Can
articles_hidden.abstract:
Introduction: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly shape how users evaluate information, form beliefs, and make decisions. Epistemic quality refers to the extent to which responses support accurate understanding, calibrated confidence, evidence-grounded beliefs, and independent reasoning. Risks extend beyond misinformation to reinforcing unsupported beliefs, expressing unwarranted certainty, and failing to challenge misleading assumptions. We developed mPACT-MIS-v1.0 to evaluate model behaviors that may support or undermine epistemic quality.

Methods: We evaluated 60 expert-authored, multi-turn conversations (642 model turns; mean 10.70 [SD 2.70], range 5–17) across ten personas and six LLMs: Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini (2.5 Flash/3 Flash Preview), GPT-5.2, Grok 4.1, LLaMA 3.3 70B, and Mistral Medium 3. Trained annotators coded model turns using four helpful and four harmful behavioral labels informed by Self-Determination Theory and user turns for risky belief or behavior expressions. Model responses were classified as helpful-only, harmful-only, mixed, or uncoded. Conversation-averaged scores (0–10; higher is better) were calculated with 95% confidence intervals from conversation-clustered bootstrapping. Additional analyses examined responses to risk, transitions, correction latency, and persona variation.

Results: Of 642 model turns, 261 (40.7%) were harmful-only, 78 (12.1%) mixed, 139 (21.7%) helpful-only, and 164 (25.5%) uncoded; 52.8% contained harmful behavior. Promoting risky beliefs or behaviors was the most frequent harmful label, while assessing risk was the least frequent helpful label (2.0%). Scores ranged from 2.60/10 (95% CI 1.68–4.04) for Mistral Medium 3 to 6.98/10 (95% CI 5.80–8.04) for Claude Sonnet 4.5, the only model with more helpful-only than harmful-only turns. Harmful behavior followed 74% of risky belief expressions and 73% of risky behavior expressions, versus 28% of turns without preceding risk expressions. Harmful responses often persisted: Claude recovered to helpful-only on 35% of transitions, versus 0–6% for four other models. Of 78 mixed responses, 77 combined a challenge to user beliefs or behaviors with harmful behavior. Performance varied substantially across personas.

Discussion: Harmful responses frequently reinforced risky beliefs or behaviors, while support for independent reasoning was less common. Persistent harmful behavior, variable recovery, and mixed responses demonstrate why epistemic safety requires evaluation beyond factual accuracy or isolated outputs. Misinformation-related risks may arise through how models engage with users' beliefs over time. mPACT-MIS-v1.0 offers a behavioral framework for identifying potential reinforcement or correction, although it does not directly measure changes in users' beliefs or decisions.

articles_hidden.title: Explicit knowledge modulates Pavlovian attentional biases
articles_hidden.authors: Francisco Garre-Frutos; Pablo Martínez-López; Adriana Ariza; Ricardo Rey-Sáez; David Luque; Miguel A. Vadillo; Felisa González
articles_hidden.abstract: Cues that signal reward can become motivational magnets, capturing attention automatically even when doing so runs counter to our goals. Once established, these Pavlovian attentional biases persist even when they no longer predict reward, which has been interpreted as an inflexible form of attentional sign-tracking. Here, we asked whether explicit knowledge can nonetheless update such biases by examining their time course after a reversal of stimulus–reward contingencies. Across three experiments (N = 216), two of them preregistered, verbal instructions about the reversal effectively abolished the bias at the onset of the reversal stage, both with (Experiment 1) and without (Experiment 2a) trial-by-trial reward feedback. In contrast, when participants were not informed of the reversal but received feedback (Experiment 2b), the bias persisted over the same initial blocks and was only gradually reversed through experience, and the extent of this reversal was associated with participants' awareness of the new contingencies. Computational modeling of a previously published dataset further suggests that explicit knowledge about the reversal prompted an immediate, model-based revaluation of the stimuli's learned values. These findings show that reversal instructions can modulate previously acquired Pavlovian attentional biases, and suggest that these biases, even if expressed automatically, are not necessarily independent of explicit knowledge.

articles_hidden.title: NFTs and digital IDs: Unexplored opportunities for psychological assessment?
articles_hidden.authors: Ian MacRae; Walter M. Yuan; Harris Eyre
articles_hidden.abstract: This article considers how non-fungible tokens (NFTs) and decentralised digital identities could be used in psychological and health assessment, beyond their better-known use in digital art markets. It outlines NFT credentials in decentralised finance, the shift from username-and-password and federated login systems to self-sovereign identity wallets, and emerging frameworks such as the EU’s ESSIF. The authors argue that these tools could let participants share psychometric, health or behavioural data while remaining in control of their information, and could help verify that participants are real people without revealing their identity. They also set out ethical challenges, including informed consent and large open behavioural datasets, and call on psychologists and the BPS to help shape professional standards.

articles_hidden.title: Development and psychometric properties of the CDI-IIIR for language assessment of 30- to 48-month-olds
articles_hidden.authors: No authors listed
articles_hidden.abstract: The Macarthur-Bates Communicative Development Inventories (CDI) are a set of widely used parent-report instruments for measuring young children’s language development. The most widely used measures for English-speaking children are the CDIs for 8-30 months. There is a strong need for both clinical and research purpose for comparable measures for three-year-olds. The previously published U.S. English CDI-III yielded norms for 30-37 months only, due to ceiling effects, and assessed limited aspects of language. Recent adaptations for Swedish and other Scandinavian languages, have used a different design and showed strong psychometric properties for children 2.5-4 years old. The current study utilizes insights from that work to revise the CDI-III for an expanded target age range, and to incorporate more aspects of language, including morphology and metalinguistic and print awareness. Results are presented for a sample of 202 children as reported on a pilot version of the new instrument, for both the full set of items and those items selected on the basis of IRT analysis for the final instrument, and also for a preliminary norming sample of 322 children utilizing the final instrument. The CDI-IIIR appears to have good reliability and developmental sensitivity across the target age range of 30 through 48 months. A larger norming sample, and validation evidence, are essential next steps.
